descriptionChirho: The noun melqachayim (dual form) denoting tongs or snuffers used in temple service — tools for trimming lamp wicks or handling hot coals. All four clusters describe the same implement with grammatical variation: possessive suffix (eng: its snuffers/tongs, arb: مَلاقِطُها, hin: उसके–चिमटे), definite plural (eng: the tongs, arb: الْمَلَاقِطُ, kor: 불집게들), bare construct (eng: its snuffers, arb: مَلاَقِطَهَا, swa: mikasi-yake), and prepositional (eng: with tongs, arb: بِمِلقَطٍ, hin: चिमटे–से). Arabic ملاقط (malaaqit), Hindi चिमटे (chimte), Korean 불집게 (buljipge), and Swahili mikasi/koleo are consistent across all clusters, confirming a single sense of a grasping/gripping temple utensil.
